PullRequest.Title: Hide migration notice after migrations are ignored
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #342834

After users ignored all migration groups, the **Review Migrations** notice and related migration shortcuts could still claim that work remained. This change filters ignored category/scope groups from every migration hint, preserves existing workspace-scoped dismissals, and clears stale availability while migration discovery refreshes.

- Shares the persisted harness, storage, category, and project ignore-key logic between the migrations page and its notice consumers.
- Keeps notice dismissal keyed to the stable workspace identity while using the active project root for workspace migration ignores.
- Recomputes the composer notice and Agents Window navigation shortcut when migrations are ignored or restored.
- Keeps ignored groups hidden for their original harness while allowing nonignored scopes, other harnesses, and restored groups to surface.
- Adds focused regression tests and a four-theme component fixture for the ignored-migrations state.

## Validation

- Passed: `npm run build-fast -- --client-only`
- Passed: `$files = git diff --name-only HEAD -- '*.ts'; npm run eslint -- $files`
- Passed, 9 tests: `.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\aiCustomization\chatCustomizationMigrationNotice.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\aiCustomization\customizationMigrationServiceImpl.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\aiCustomization\aiCustomizationManagementEditor.test.ts --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\chat\test\browser\newChatMigrationNotice.test.ts --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\sessions\test\browser\customizationsToolbar.test.ts --grep "ignored migration|migration availability|dismissal persists|customizations change|migrations sidebar entry|active project root"`
- Passed: `npm run typecheck-client`
- Passed: `npm run valid-layers-check`
- Passed for Dark, Light, High Contrast Dark, and High Contrast Light: `npx @vscode/component-explorer-cli render --project "test\componentFixtures\component-explorer.json" --fixture-id-regex "^sessions/chat/newWidget/newChatWidget/MigrationsIgnored/" --workers 1`
- Passed: Repeated final fixture capture produced identical SHA-256 hashes for all four themes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening or switching the chat/new-chat composer while a migration notice is eligible
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Notice construction synchronously hides the element, then starts computeMigrationHint asynchronously. Composer rendering and input remain usable; only notice availability waits for discovery.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover prompt, instruction, agent, and skill files through IPromptsService.listPromptFiles across user and workspace locations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to five prompt-type list requests per hint computation; duplicate types share cached/coalesced promises in PromptsService, so warm calls reuse results and cold calls scan once per type.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same computeMigrationHint call and prompt-file discovery ran before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the composer critical path but required before the migration notice can appear.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query agent-host plugin marketplaces when configured marketplace candidates exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one agent-host listPluginMarketplaces request per hint computation; skipped when no configured marketplace candidates/provider exists.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same plugin-marketplace branch ran before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only notice availability waits; composer interaction does not.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Build the MCP migration plan, including grouped source configuration reads and secret checks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One plan per hint computation; source file reads scale with distinct MCP source files/roots rather than candidate count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same MCP discovery branch ran before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only notice availability waits; cancellation discards stale computations.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of prompt files, distinct prompt types, MCP source files, and configured marketplaces. The added ignored-group list is bounded by homepage categories times two storage scopes and filtering is O(candidates × bounded groups).
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: computeMigrationHint retains the pre-existing Promise.all of five migration categories. Context changes and ignored-group storage changes cancel stale consumers; underlying operations receive cancellation tokens. One notice instance issues one computation per relevant observable change.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Prompt lists use per-type positive promise caching and coalescing, invalidated by file/provider events; agent source-folder readiness is cached per session. Marketplace listing and MCP planning are recomputed per hint request. The PR does not defeat these caches.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed call sites and all transitive migration branches were traced; no new boundary is added to composer startup.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Agent-host IPC and filesystem duration vary by provider and workspace size, but the diff does not increase initial-load cardinality. Ignore/project changes are infrequent user/workspace events.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The PR adds bounded ignored-group lookup/filtering and refreshes after explicit ignore/project changes while preserving existing asynchronous discovery and fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Showing the Sessions customizations navigation shortcut and reacting to ignored/restored migration groups
Scenarios.CriticalPath: When the treatment navigation is enabled, the state starts one asynchronous migration hint computation and temporarily clears availability. Sessions rendering and navigation remain usable; only the migration badge/shortcut waits.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run the same prompt-file and MCP migration discovery used by composer notices.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One computation per enabled-state/session/harness/configuration/customization/project-root/ignored-group change; each computation retains the five grouped category branches described above.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Initial and customization-triggered discovery already existed; the diff adds refreshes specifically for active-project-root and ignored-group changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required only for the migration shortcut state, not sessions-list progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Potentially list configured agent-host plugin marketplaces.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one request per refresh when configured candidates and a management provider exist. An ignore/restore action can also refresh an active notice, yielding at most one request per active consumer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The IPC branch was already part of every hint computation; the PR adds a bounded invocation on explicit ignore/restore changes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Active navigation consumers and explicit ignored-group changes, not session-list row count. Effective ignored keys are at most the supported category/scope combinations for the current harness/project.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each navigation state serially replaces its autorun generation and cancellation token. It may overlap with one active migration notice because these are independent consumers; there is no per-row or per-session fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm prompt-file discovery is reused by the shared prompts service. Ignored keys are read once into a Set per refresh; there is no growing in-memory cache. Negative hint results are not cached, matching prior behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: ownership is one state per SessionsView and enablement is gated by the treatment presentation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact overlap depends on which composer/notice is mounted and whether plugin marketplaces are configured. Ignore and restore are explicit, low-frequency actions.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The additional refresh gives immediate badge correctness and is bounded to infrequent state changes; it does not scale with sessions or rows.

Scenarios.Scenario: Ignoring or restoring migration categories in the customization management editor
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After confirmation, the editor updates profile storage and refreshes migration UI synchronously. Notice/navigation consumers react asynchronously; the editor does not wait for their migration discovery.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize the ignored migration key Set into profile storage.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One profile-storage write per ignore or restore action; payload size is bounded by harness/category/scope combinations accumulated by the user.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The editor previously serialized the same groupKeys array directly to the same profile key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The storage write is on the action path, but the extracted helper preserves the prior write shape and target.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of ignored harness/project/category keys retained in profile storage. Each user action adds/removes one or selected keys; normal cardinality is small and no new duplicate keys are possible because Set is used.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single synchronous storage update fans out to mounted consumers, each with cancellation-aware async refresh. The editor's own UI refresh remains immediate and local.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is introduced. Reads deserialize the stored object and construct a Set, preserving prior editor behavior; consumers independently read the latest value on the storage event.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: helper extraction is behavior-equivalent for storage, and all production writers were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Profiles can retain keys for multiple projects/harnesses, but realistic storage size is small and the PR does not change retention policy or representation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression. Serialization/allocation is unchanged, and the new reactive work is bounded to explicit ignore/restore actions.

Scenarios.Scenario: Computing a migration hint with ignored groups
Scenarios.CriticalPath: All enabled migration categories are discovered in parallel, then candidates are filtered by the bounded ignored-group descriptors before counts/message generation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Prompt and MCP discovery executes before ignored candidates are filtered.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Same category/file boundary count as before; ignored groups do not add filesystem calls. Candidate filtering performs bounded in-memory comparisons.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same full discovery happened before ignored-group support; only post-discovery candidate filtering is new.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for hint completion, as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Plugin marketplace listing executes before ignored marketplace candidates are filtered.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one request per hint computation when configured candidates exist, unchanged from before.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The marketplace listing was already unconditional for configured candidates within each hint computation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for hint completion but not host UI progress.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total migration candidates. The new `some` checks multiply candidate filtering by a descriptor list bounded by supported categories and user/local scopes, so it cannot grow with history independently of candidates.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Five category computations remain parallel via Promise.all; the PR neither raises category concurrency nor introduces per-candidate async work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No candidate cache is added or invalidated. Existing prompt caches remain effective; ignored groups are supplied as immutable per-refresh snapshots.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the implementation was compared directly before/after and no expensive operation moved into the candidate loops.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Candidate collections can vary by workspace, but the added CPU/allocation consists of five filtered arrays and bounded comparisons, while pre-existing discovery dominates.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The added allocation/CPU is linear in existing candidate collections with a tiny bounded multiplier and enables required count filtering.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 14 changed files and every diff page. Traced composer notices, Sessions navigation, editor ignore/restore storage, migration discovery, prompt caches, MCP filesystem work, and agent-host marketplace IPC. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression or qualifying regression fix was found.
